capabilities: Sync selected vault files with one GitHub repository and branch
Merge Markdown changed on both devices with a three-way merge and conflict copies
Filter pull and push by extension and ignore path prefixes
Push automatically after a debounce and pull by polling while the app is in the foreground
Resolve conflicts explicitly with keep-local or keep-remote choices
disambiguation: Not a Git client; it never runs Git locally and speaks only to the GitHub REST API, so there is no local history, branching, or force push.
extras: Not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Installation requires building with Node.js 18+ and npm, then copying three runtime files into the vault manually, including on iOS. Free with an optional Buy Me a Coffee donation; no paid tiers. Stores tokens in Obsidian secret storage on 1.11.4+, in plain text in older versions.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to sync a vault with a GitHub repository without shelling out to a Git binary, which is impractical on iOS, and Obsidian Sync requires a paid subscription.

relations.evidence: synchronizes selected vault files with a single GitHub repository through GitHub's Git Database REST API

requires.name: GitHub account with a fine-grained personal access token (Contents: Read and write)

summary: Syncs selected vault files with a single GitHub repository via the GitHub REST API, including three-way merge and conflict copies, on desktop and iOS.
